2027-06-15.title: Memory of the first church built in the name of the Mother of God · Tuesday of the fourth week after Pentecost
readings: In whatever condition you were called, there remain with God
The true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth
2027-06-15.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Fourth Sunday after Pentecost. The Panchangam keeps the memory of the founding of the first church in the name of the holy Mother of God; it does not say where or when that church was built. The Apostles' Fast begins tomorrow.
2027-06-15.verse: But the hour is coming, and is now here, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father seeks such as these to worship him.
theo: Today the Panchangam asks us to remember the founding of the first church built in the name of the holy Mother of God. It gives no place and no date, and we do not need to supply them. What it wants us to remember is enough: very early, the disciples of Jesus began to raise houses of prayer and to give them the name of his Mother. Think how many churches in our own villages and towns are called St Mary's, Marth Mariam, the church of the Mother of God. Every one of them is a grandchild of that first church. And the Gospel the Church gives us for this memory is, surprisingly, a word of Jesus about the place of worship. At the well of Sychar the Samaritan woman raises the old dispute between her people and the Jews: is God to be worshipped on this mountain or in Jerusalem? Jesus answers: “Woman, believe me, the hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.” He does not despise the faith of Israel; he says plainly that “salvation is from the Jews.” But he announces something new: “the hour is coming, and is now here, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father seeks such as these to worship him.”

Does this mean that church buildings no longer matter? Not at all. Worship “in spirit and truth” does not mean a vague prayer anywhere and nowhere. The Spirit is the Holy Spirit poured out at Pentecost, and the Truth is Christ himself, who says to the woman, “I am he, the one who is speaking to you.” True worship is worship offered in Christ and through the Spirit, and that happens above all when the Body of Christ gathers around the altar. Solomon knew that no house could hold God: “Even heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain you, much less this house that I have built!” A church is not a box for God; it is a home for his people, a sign on earth of the Father's house. St Augustine, preaching on this Gospel, said: if you want to pray in a temple, pray within yourself, but first become a temple of God (Tractates on John 15, in substance). That is why a church is fitting for the Mother of God. She was the first temple of the new covenant, the one in whom the Word dwelt for nine months. St Cyril of Alexandria, preaching at Ephesus in 431, greeted her as the Mother of God, the temple that cannot be destroyed, holding him whom no place can hold (Homily at Ephesus, in substance). A church that bears her name does not compete with her Son; like her at Cana it says, “Do whatever he tells you.”

The Epistle brings the lesson home. The Christians of Corinth were tempted to think that holiness meant changing their circumstances: the circumcised wanted to hide it, the uncircumcised wanted to be circumcised, the married wondered whether to separate. Paul says: stop looking elsewhere. “Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing; but obeying the commandments of God is everything.” And again: “In whatever condition you were called, brothers and sisters, there remain with God.” God is to be worshipped in spirit and truth in the church, and then in the kitchen, the paddy field, the shop, the office and the classroom that has just reopened after the summer. The holy Mother of God herself lived for years in an ordinary house at Nazareth, cooking, drawing water and keeping the words of God in her heart. Her first sanctuary was a home. So today, thank God for the church where you were baptised, and then make your own house and work a place where the Father finds a true worshipper.
outline: Ask: when I come to church, do I bring my whole life with me, or only an hour?
Jesus at the well: the Father seeks worshippers in the Spirit and in Christ, the Truth.
Point 2 · A house named for the Mother of God
Churches are homes for God's people, not boxes for God; Mary was the first temple of the Word.
Point 3 · Remain with God where you were called
Worship continues at home and at work, as it did in the house of Nazareth.
“In whatever condition you were called, brothers and sisters, there remain with God.”
live: Come ten minutes early to the next Holy Qurbono and spend them in silence before the altar, asking the Holy Spirit to make your worship true.
Begin the ordinary work of today with a short prayer offering it to God, and end it with thanks.
2027-06-15.prayer: Father in heaven, you seek true worshippers who will worship you in spirit and truth. Pour your Holy Spirit on us, who gather in houses of prayer built in your name and in the name of the holy Mother of God. As she welcomed your Word and became his first dwelling, let us welcome him in the Holy Qurbono and carry him into our homes and our work. Wherever you have called us, keep us with you, faithful to your commandments and glad in your service. Through Jesus Christ our Lord, who lives and reigns with you and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: Every church is built for its altar: there, in the Holy Qurbono, the Word who once dwelt in the womb of the holy Virgin comes to dwell among us under the forms of bread and wine, and we become the worshippers the Father seeks.
conn: John 4:21–26 is the heart of the conversation at Jacob's well; before it Jesus offers living water (John 4:10–14), and after it many in the town believe (John 4:39–42).
A house too small for God.
1 Kings 8:27: Solomon confesses that the temple cannot contain God; the church building is a sign of his presence among his people, not a container.
The first dwelling of the Word.
John 1:14 and Luke 1:35: the Word became flesh in the womb of the Virgin; the Council of Ephesus (431) confessed her as Mother of God.
fathers: If you wish to pray in a temple, pray within yourself; but first become a temple of God, for he hears in his temple the one who prays (Tractates on John 15, in substance).
Hail, Mary, Mother of God, temple that cannot be destroyed, who held within you the One whom no place can hold (Homily at Ephesus, in substance).
magis: The worship in Spirit and truth of the New Covenant is not tied exclusively to one place; but when the faithful gather, they are the living stones built into a spiritual house, and their churches show the Church living in that place.
The visible church is a symbol of the Father's house towards which the People of God is journeying, where the Father will wipe every tear from their eyes.
Called in the Gospels the mother of Jesus, Mary is acclaimed by Elizabeth as the mother of my Lord; the Church confesses that she is truly Mother of God.

quick: The Panchangam remembers the founding of the first church in the name of the holy Mother of God.
Jesus tells the Samaritan woman: the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth.
St Paul: in whatever condition you were called, remain there with God.
2027-06-15.action: Visit a church today, even for two minutes, and pray before the altar.
2027-06-15.question: Is my worship only in the church, or does it continue in my home and my work?

family.explain: Jesus met a woman at a well who asked him where people should pray to God. Jesus said that God the Father looks for people who pray with the Holy Spirit and with true hearts. We build churches so that God's family can gather and pray together, and many churches are named after Mother Mary, because she was the first home of baby Jesus. But we must also pray in our own home.
family.intention: We thank God for our parish church and pray that our home may also be a place of prayer.
family.ask: Ask: “Which church were you baptised in, and who is it named after?”

illus: An old woman in a village near Pathanamthitta walked every morning for fifty years to St Mary's church, two kilometres along the canal. When her knees finally would not carry her, she set a small picture of the Mother of God with the Child on a shelf near the kitchen door, and when she heard the church bell across the fields she stopped her work and prayed. Her grandson once asked her whether she missed the church. She said: the church is far, but its Lord is near; and the Mother always takes me to her Son. On Sundays, when the family carried her to the Qurbono in a chair, she wept with joy at the altar. The parish priest said she had understood both halves of the Gospel: the house of God and the worship in spirit and truth.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, you make us true worshippers of the Father. Teach us to pray in your house and in our homes, with the holy Mother of God who kept the word in her heart. Amen.
share: The true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth (John 4:23). What helps me to pray truly, and what distracts me?
Even heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain you, much less this house that I have built (1 Kings 8:27). What does my parish church mean to me?
In whatever condition you were called, brothers and sisters, there remain with God (1 Corinthians 7:24). Where is God asking me to be faithful just now?
pm.resp: Father, make us your true worshippers.
interc: For the Church throughout the world, that her churches may be houses of prayer for all peoples.
For our parish church and all churches named after the holy Mother of God, that those who pray in them may find her Son.
For those who cannot come to church because of age, illness or distance, that the Lord may visit them at home.
For students and teachers as the new school year begins, that their work may be offered to God.
For Christians of all Churches who honour the Mother of God, that she may lead us to unity in her Son.
pm.close: Lord God, Mary, the Mother of your Son, became the first dwelling of your Word, and the first church built in her name has many children in our land. Make us living temples of your Spirit, faithful in your house and faithful in our daily work, and bring us at last to your house in heaven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today the Panchangam remembers the founding of the first church built in the name of the holy Mother of God. We do not know where it stood. But we know its children: so many churches in our land carry her name. And the Gospel today is about worship. Jesus says to the Samaritan woman: the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth (John 4:23).

Worship in spirit and truth is not prayer without a church. The Spirit is the Holy Spirit of Pentecost, and the Truth is Jesus himself, who says: I am he, the one who is speaking to you (John 4:26). We worship in spirit and truth above all when we gather at the altar for the Holy Qurbono. The church building is not a box for God. Solomon said that heaven itself cannot contain him (1 Kings 8:27). The church is a home for God's family.

Why name a church after Mary? Because she was the first house of God among us. The Word of God lived in her womb. A church with her name does not take us away from Jesus. Mary says what she said at Cana: do whatever he tells you (John 2:5).

And St Paul adds: in whatever condition you were called, brothers and sisters, there remain with God (1 Corinthians 7:24). Our worship must not stay inside the church. Like the holy Mother of God in her house at Nazareth, let us make our homes, our fields, our offices and our classrooms places where God is honoured. Amen.
kids: Children, what is the name of your parish church? Many churches in Kerala are named after Mother Mary. Do you know why? Because Mary was the very first home of Jesus. Before any church was built, Jesus lived inside his mother, close to her heart. Today Jesus tells us that God loves people who pray with true hearts. So when you go to church, pray with all your heart. And at home, before you study or play, say a little prayer too. Then your home also becomes a small church.

intro: Theme: “The true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth.”
On the memory of the first church built in the name of the holy Mother of God: worship in spirit and truth, the house of God, and faithfulness where we were called.

sub: Not this mountain, not that one.
The Spirit of Pentecost and Christ the Truth.
The altar at the heart of true worship.
q: For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering
I appeal to you therefore, brothers and sisters, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship.
points.apply: At the next Holy Qurbono, join your voice to the prayers and responses instead of only listening.

points.h: A house named for the Mother of God
sub: Mary, the first dwelling of the Word.
A church that points to her Son.
q: But will God indeed dwell on the earth? Even heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain you, much less this house that I have built!
Surely, from now on all generations will call me blessed
points.apply: Learn the story of your parish church this week: when it was built, and why it bears its name.

points.h: Remain with God where you were called
q: and what does the Lord require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
And whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.
points.apply: Choose one ordinary task you dislike and do it today carefully, as an offering to God.

concl: The first church built in the name of the Mother of God has many children, and every one of them exists for the worship the Father seeks.
Worship that begins at the altar continues in the house, the field and the classroom.
2027-06-15.resolve: Worship the Father in spirit and truth in his house, and remain with him wherever he has placed you.
